title: Browser navigation policy refusals
pins: Which URLs a browser policy refuses, and under WHICH CODE, in every language. The code is the contract — a consumer switches on it to decide whether to retry, widen a list, or surface a hard stop. The message is deliberately not pinned; the three implementations word these differently on purpose, and a test over the prose holds every language to a translation and reddens on a wording improvement that changed nothing.
scope: The URL policy's refusal decision and its code. It does NOT cover what the engine does once a URL is allowed, the page content that comes back, or the harness binding (G-19). A green run here means the policy refuses the right URLs under the right code, and nothing about what happens after one is admitted.
findings: All twelve rows now agree, and three of them did not until G-21 was closed. url-0005, url-0006 and url-0007 — the cloud metadata endpoint, loopback, and an RFC 1918 address, each explicitly allow-listed — were refused by every language from the start, so nothing was ever unprotected; what differed was the NAME. The reference said `private_network_refused` and exposed it as `$refused->reason`, both ports said `private_address_refused` and exposed it as `.code`, so a consumer switching on the code fell through to its default branch in one direction and read an SSRF refusal as an unknown failure. The reference moved, not the ports: the check is per-ADDRESS rather than per-network, and `.code` is what every other error surface in this ecosystem carries. Closing it also turned up a second emitter the register had not predicted — the Playwright sidecar raises this code on its post-DNS check, and `PlaywrightSidecarEngine` passes it to the caller verbatim, so the reference would otherwise have disagreed with ITSELF on the runtime path that actually resists rebinding. Read the agreement narrowly: this corpus compares languages, so a bug all three shared would look exactly like the green it now shows, which is why each runner also asserts the refusal happened rather than only comparing strings.
